Get started with FunMel

Mitra Ghotbi

Source: vignettes/FunMel.Rmd
FunMel.Rmd

What the package measures

The standard assay has four Zymoseptoria tritici target colonies around another fungus. The central fungal core and its peripheral hyphal growth are separated from Zymo before target measurements. These regions represent image-based fungal tissue candidates. They are not an inhibition boundary or evidence of pigment diffusion. The software cannot distinguish species or microscopic hyphae from colour alone. Contact between organisms may require manual interpretation.

Melanization index is MI = 100 - CIELAB L*, from 0 (white) to 100 (black). It measures image darkness, not melanin concentration. Calibration, exposure, illumination and segmentation affect the result.

There are two complementary measurements:

Measurement Pixel selection Where to find it
Whole-colony MI All eligible interior pixels colonies: MI_min, MI_mean, MI_max
Optional circular spots A chosen number of spatially distributed ROIs spots, plus MI_spot_mean/min/max in colonies

The default matched coefficients use whole-colony MI_mean. Spots are optional subsamples, not additional biological replicates.

Install and open the package 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)

R >= 4.1 and a compilation toolchain are needed: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick libraries on Linux. Restart R before updating a loaded installation. To include the installed vignette:

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel",
                        build_vignettes=TRUE, dependencies=TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package="FunMel")

Pandoc is required to build vignettes and is normally supplied by RStudio.

A first runnable image example

This simulated image demonstrates the commands without external files. It is a computational example, not biological validation of real photographs.

sim <- simulate_plate(width=400,height=400,seed=7)
result <- analyze_plate(sim$image, n_spots=3, spot_radius_mm=0.4,
                        n_boot=20, verbose=FALSE)
knitr::kable(result$colonies[,c("colony_id","MI_min","MI_mean","MI_max",
                               "n_spots_measured","MI_spot_mean","spot_status")],digits=2)
colony_id MI_min MI_mean MI_max n_spots_measured MI_spot_mean spot_status
x TL 24.46 46.32 79.40 3 41.56 ok
x1 TR 39.23 52.24 79.12 3 50.12 ok
x2 BR 41.18 58.46 79.69 3 61.63 ok
x3 BL 23.68 41.14 79.18 3 38.61 ok 
plot_qc(result)

White numbered circles show the optional sampling ROIs. Inspect them along with the colony and central-growth masks before using results. Controls use plate_layout(centre="none"); the default confrontation uses centre="fungus".

Follow the real 14-day photographs: step by step

The package includes eight original photographs in extdata/14-days. They form two complete sets, each with one control and three independent confrontation plates. Four Zymo colonies are measured within each plate. No separate download or ZIP extraction is needed.

Set Control photograph Treatment photographs
A60_2_14_days 2026_10_02_99_41.JPG ...38.JPG, ...39.JPG, ...40.JPG
B20_2_14_days 2026_10_02_99_45.JPG ...42.JPG, ...43.JPG, ...44.JPG

Step 1. Prepare the example project 

library(FunMel)
photos14 <- system.file("extdata", "14-days", package="FunMel")
stopifnot(nzchar(photos14))
project14 <- prepare_experiment(photos14, "FunMel_14_day_project")
project14$metadata_file

The last line prints the location of plate_metadata.csv. Open that file in Excel, LibreOffice or a text editor. Edit the project copy, not the installed example. Keep it as CSV when saving. Use a new project folder name to start over; existing projects are not overwritten.

Step 2. Check the experimental metadata

There are eight rows: two control plates and six treatment plates. Check every row against laboratory records:

  1. Preserve file, relative_file and the unique plate_id.
  2. Verify treatment and set_id. Each control and its three treatment plates share one set_id. Enter the control once; do not duplicate it per treatment.
  3. Use centre_model="none" for controls and centre_model="fungus" for confrontations. Check day=14, replicate labels and recorded strain/medium.
  4. Set metadata_confirmed to TRUE for verified rows, then save the CSV. This confirmation is required to protect treatment-to-control matching.

Folder codes and the supplied fungus="hm83" field require biological interpretation from records. The example does not invent strain, medium or partner identities. Additional metadata columns are retained automatically. Leave qc_pass=FALSE until a plate’s image analysis has been reviewed; this flag is an optional record of QC approval, not a default calculation gate.

Step 3. Measure the photographs

Enter the actual outer dish diameter in millimetres when prompted. All images in this run use that scale; use separate runs for different dish sizes.

dish_mm <- as.numeric(readline("Actual outer dish diameter in mm: "))
stopifnot(length(dish_mm)==1L, is.finite(dish_mm), dish_mm>0)
result14 <- run_experiment(
  project14, dish_diameter_mm=dish_mm, max_dim=1200,
  n_spots=5, spot_radius_mm=0.4
)
result14$failed
project14$qc_dir

This keeps whole-colony MI and requests five circular sampling spots per target colony. Omit n_spots and spot_radius_mm for whole-colony measurements alone. Check spot_status: five non-overlapping spots may not fit every usable colony. The default final coefficient uses whole-colony MI_mean, not the spot means. Resolve any rows in result14$failed before finalization.

Step 4. Inspect the QC images

The last command prints the QC folder. Open it in Finder or File Explorer and inspect all eight PNGs. Check that:

  • Target outlines follow the visible Zymo colony boundaries.
  • Central fungal tissue, surrounding hyphae, shadows and agar are excluded from target measurements; controls have no central fungus assigned.
  • Optional sampling circles lie inside the correct colonies. Review scale, exposure, illumination, insufficient-spot and other warnings.

Correct unsuitable settings and rerun Step 3 when necessary. A new run resets qc_pass=FALSE because the new masks have not been reviewed. Do not rerun image analysis merely to load an edited review CSV.

QC approval is optional by default. You may record qc_pass=TRUE in the CSV for each acceptable, reviewed plate. If any flags remain FALSE, are missing or unknown, finalization warns and continues. It keeps the flags unchanged, reports unconfirmed QC and labels the figure caption. This is a reminder to review before interpreting or publishing, not automatic validation of the masks.

Step 5. Calculate and export the results 

reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14)
reviewed14$melanization_coefficient
reviewed14$qc_review
reviewed14$assessment$status

metadata_confirmed=TRUE is still required for each included row. A warning about unconfirmed image QC does not stop the default calculation. A warning about fewer than two plates in a set-treatment cell means that this example has one control per set: it supports descriptive ratios, not inferential tests. The four colonies per plate and the individual spots are subsamples, not extra independent controls.

Open these files in FunMel_14_day_project:

File Contents
metadata_used.csv Complete metadata, including original QC flags and custom fields
qc_review_status.csv Whether QC was confirmed and which plates remain unconfirmed
colonies.csv, spots.csv Colony summaries and individual sampling ROIs
melanization_coefficient.csv Treatment MI divided by its own set’s control MI, with QC status
treatment_comparison.pdf, .svg, .png Exported comparison figure; caption identifies unconfirmed QC

A ratio above 1 means darker target colonies than the matching control; below 1 means lighter. This is image darkness, not measured melanin concentration. Each treatment occurs in one set, so batch effects can remain confounded with treatment even after control adjustment. Review design, warnings and diagnostics before drawing biological conclusions.

Optional strict QC: after setting qc_pass=TRUE only for acceptable, reviewed plates and saving the CSV, use:

reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14, require_qc=TRUE)

Strict mode stops if any included plate lacks explicit QC approval. The default is require_qc=FALSE; it does not require you to change QC flags to calculate.

Step 6. Resume after restarting R 

library(FunMel)
project14 <- readRDS("FunMel_14_day_project/project.rds")
result14 <- readRDS(project14$result_file)
# After editing and saving metadata, reuse the saved measurements:
reviewed14 <- finish_experiment(project14)

Use the full project path if your working directory has changed. A companion R script is at system.file("examples", "walkthrough_14_days.R", package="FunMel"); open it and run each numbered section separately.

For your own images, replace photos14 in Step 1 with a photograph folder path, or file.choose() to select a ZIP. Supply metadata that describes those images; the bundled eight-row template applies only to the eight example photographs. The original 20-photo archive needs a matching 20-row metadata table and is not interchangeable with this eight-photo teaching subset.

Analyze an experiment in three stages

Stage 1: prepare photographs and metadata

A ZIP can contain any number of batches, each with control and treatment subfolders. For example:

Folder Images
day8/batch1/control/ Control plates for this day and batch
day8/batch1/fungus_A/ Replicate treatment plates using those controls
day8/batch2/control/ A different matching control set
day8/batch2/fungus_B/ Replicate treatment plates for batch 2

An enclosing ZIP folder is supported. Images with identical basenames in different folders remain distinct through their relative paths. A unique plate_metadata.csv inside the ZIP can supply the design. Otherwise folder labels propose a template for review. Only explicit control or controls folders count as proposed controls; customize control_folders if necessary. An ambiguous folder layout leaves treatment labels blank rather than guessing.

project <- prepare_experiment(file.choose(), "FunMel_project")
# Or supply a directory:
# project <- prepare_experiment("path/to/photos", "FunMel_project")
project$metadata_file

Open that CSV in a spreadsheet editor. Preserve file, relative_file and plate_id. Verify set_id, treatment and centre_model. Use control and centre_model="none" for a control; use the experimental treatment name and centre_model="fungus" for fungal confrontations. The optional partner_type records biology separately from the computational recipe. Set metadata_confirmed=TRUE after checking assignments; leave qc_pass=FALSE until reviewing image masks. Both columns are present in the template.

Each treatment uses its own control set. One control and three independent treatment plates require four metadata rows with the same set_id. The single control is entered once, not copied three times:

metadata_example <- data.frame(
  plate_id=c("C1","T1","T2","T3"),set_id="batch1",
  treatment=c("control",rep("fungus_A",3)),
  centre_model=c("none",rep("fungus",3)),
  metadata_confirmed=FALSE,qc_pass=FALSE)
knitr::kable(metadata_example)
plate_id set_id treatment centre_model metadata_confirmed qc_pass
C1 batch1 control none FALSE FALSE
T1 batch1 fungus_A fungus FALSE FALSE
T2 batch1 fungus_A fungus FALSE FALSE
T3 batch1 fungus_A fungus FALSE FALSE

Different strains, days or media require separate set IDs and explicit context columns (zymo_strain, day, medium). Add and fill the relevant columns in the CSV; folder paths alone do not define statistical context variables. Finalization separates recorded contexts into indexed output folders. Repeated photographs of the same plate on different days are repeated measures, not independent replicates; the built-in model does not estimate a longitudinal response.

Stage 2: analyze, then inspect every plate 

# Whole-colony measurements only:
result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm=90)

# Alternative: retain whole-colony MI and add five circular spots per target:
result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm=90,
                         n_spots=5, spot_radius_mm=0.4)

Run one of the alternatives. The dish diameter is the actual outer dish diameter; do not assume 90 mm if a different dish was used. The project saves measurements, QC figures and image_analysis.rds. Failures remain in failed.csv. Coefficients are calculated during finalization after experimental metadata confirmation; unconfirmed image QC warns by default.

Inspect all QC PNGs in project$qc_dir. Check target outlines, central core and hyphal growth, sampling circles, exposure, scale and illumination warnings. Correct unsuitable settings and rerun if necessary. Each new run resets qc_pass=FALSE so changed masks require a new review. Save per-plate review decisions in the CSV. metadata_confirmed must be logical TRUE for every included plate. Unconfirmed qc_pass warns and continues by default; finish_experiment(project, require_qc=TRUE) instead requires explicit QC approval. Do not mark unresolved masks as passed merely to obtain a number.

Stage 3: finalize and export 

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)

Finalization loads the saved image analysis and reviewed CSV. It requires confirmed experimental metadata, exact plate-ID matching and no unresolved failed images. Image QC warns by default; require_qc=TRUE makes QC approval mandatory. Editing metadata review flags does not repeat image processing. Changing segmentation settings requires a new image analysis.

Outputs include colonies.csv, spots.csv, profiles.csv, plates.csv, melanization_coefficient.csv, per-plate ratios, saved assessment and session information. Comparison figures are exported as PDF, SVG and 600-dpi PNG, with statistics CSVs. When context columns vary, consult context_index.csv and its separate context folders for figures and assessment objects.

To resume after restarting R:

project <- readRDS("FunMel_project/project.rds")
result <- readRDS(project$result_file)
# After editing the review CSV:
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)

Choose and interpret sampling spots

n_spots is the requested number per target colony; spot_radius_mm sets ROI size. Farthest-point placement gives reproducible spatial spread, beginning near the eligible-mask centroid. ROIs cannot overlap and must lie entirely within the usable, edge-excluded target mask. Specular/saturated pixels are excluded. This is a spatial sample, not a probability sample or a guarantee that a few spots represent the entire colony.

If the placement algorithm cannot fit the requested ROIs, the achieved spots remain available for inspection, spot_status="insufficient_space", and the colony’s spot summary is NA. Adjust count/radius consistently across compared plates and rerun; changing only selected colonies can change the estimand. Small ROIs must span at least one working-image pixel in radius. Very small ROIs and raw extrema are particularly sensitive to image noise.

knitr::kable(head(result$spots),digits=2)
plate_id colony_id spot_id x_px y_px spot_radius_mm n_pixels MI_mean MI_min MI_max L_mean
plate TL 1 141 141 0.4 9 48.18 44.31 52.33 51.82
plate TL 2 116 122 0.4 9 49.51 47.11 51.35 50.49
plate TL 3 167 126 0.4 9 26.98 24.46 28.58 73.02
plate TR 1 260 141 0.4 9 49.66 46.70 54.90 50.34
plate TR 2 234 125 0.4 9 49.65 43.89 76.50 50.35
plate TR 3 289 133 0.4 9 51.04 45.87 75.80 48.96

In spots, each ROI has pixel-level MI_min/mean/max. In colonies, MI_spot_min/mean/max summarize the spot means, with equal weight per spot. The whole-colony MI_min/mean/max use all eligible interior pixels, and do not change when spots are requested. Minima/maxima are observed extrema, not error bars or confidence intervals. Spatial block-bootstrap intervals are conditional on the image and mask and do not describe biological plate replication.

For a prespecified spot-based descriptive analysis:

spot_coefficients <- melanization_coefficient(reviewed, response="MI_spot_mean")

Keep the measurement method explicit. The default final assessment and figures use whole-colony MI; spots are not automatically substituted into that model.

Matched coefficients and statistical assessment

A plate’s MI is the arithmetic mean of its target-colony MI_mean values. The melanization coefficient is the mean treatment plate MI divided by the mean control plate MI from the same set_id. Plates are equally weighted, and a shared control remains one control. Ratios describe darkness indices, not ratios of melanin concentrations. MI differences and ratios answer different questions; neither proves an effect on pigment biochemistry.

The following dataset is synthetic and has three independent plates per control/treatment cell in three matched sets:

demo <- example_experiment(seed=42)
assessment <- assess_experiment(demo)
knitr::kable(assessment$coefficients[,c("set_id","treatment",
                                      "melanization_coefficient")],digits=3)
set_id treatment melanization_coefficient
S1 fungus_A 1.105
S1 fungus_B 1.248
S2 fungus_A 1.154
S2 fungus_B 1.360
S3 fungus_A 1.113
S3 fungus_B 1.224 
assessment$status
#> [1] "ok"
plot_treatment_comparison(demo)

Control plates use outlined squares and treatment plates use coloured circles. Bars span between-plate SD, not inferential CIs. Coefficient SD is conditional on the shared control mean and excludes denominator uncertainty. The separate model contrast covariance retains shared-control uncertainty for inference.

With one control and three treatment plates per set, descriptive coefficients are available but the built-in inference guard is not met. lme4/lmerTest models require adequate independent plate replication, acceptable convergence, non-singular fits and suitable residuals. Spots, pixels, rings and target colonies are nested measurements; none creates extra independent plates. Sparse or problematic designs return an explicit descriptive-only status. Inspect assessment$diagnostics and the inferential tables rather than interpreting absence of a p value as absence of an effect.

Metadata columns are preserved

Templates include file, relative_file, plate_id, set_id, treatment, centre_model, partner_type, fungus, zymo_strain, medium, day, replicate, photo_date, notes, metadata_confirmed and qc_pass. Experimental values are left blank when unknown; both review flags start as FALSE. Additional user-defined columns are retained, including their names and values. A new image-analysis run resets qc_pass to FALSE; review the new measurements. Default finalization warns and continues without changing these flags. Use require_qc=TRUE when QC approval must be mandatory.

A context column (day, medium or zymo_strain) may be entirely blank when not recorded. Once any value is entered, complete that column for all plates and keep it constant within each matching set. Do not leave a varying context unrecorded to combine incompatible experiments.

The full table is stored in result$metadata and exported as metadata_used.csv. Additional fields are also attached to measurement tables by plate_id. If a metadata name conflicts with a measured column, the measurement is protected and the metadata copy receives a metadata_ prefix in that output table. The original names remain unchanged in the full metadata table.

Resolve common problems

Situation Action
Missing/blank treatment labels Complete the metadata; folder proposals are not biological proof
Missing control Assign the actual relevant control within each set; never borrow a different batch’s control
Duplicate photograph basenames Preserve relative_file, which includes batch folders
Requested spots do not fit Inspect spot_status; adjust settings consistently and reanalyze
Central hyphae overlap a target Review separation and consider manual analysis if the photograph cannot resolve it
qc_pass remains FALSE Default finalization warns and continues, retaining unconfirmed status. Inspect QC before interpretation; optionally record reviewed decisions or enforce require_qc=TRUE.
Changed segmentation settings Rerun image analysis; old review flags do not validate new masks
Descriptive-only assessment Review the replication/design and model diagnostics

More examples and algorithm details 

source(system.file("examples","01_image_quickstart.R",package="FunMel"))
source(system.file("examples","02_coefficient_arithmetic.R",package="FunMel"))
source(system.file("examples","05_project_workflow.R",package="FunMel"))

The bundled 14-day measurement tables are a provisional measured case study with two sets, each containing one control and three treatment plates. Their experimental assignments and masks require review; they are not a validated biological reference or a basis for claiming general accuracy. Synthetic tests verify computational behavior, not biological discrimination across all fungi.

The separate guides/FunMel_overview.md describes the image features, watershed separation, spot sampling and matched-set inference. ImageJ/Fiji remains useful for manual ROI analysis and difficult boundaries; no superiority in accuracy or speed is claimed.
